1000.author: yuanzhou75
1000.body:
## Context

Split from #439 (closed). The two non-UI asks from that issue are already done: unbuffered long-running launches (#611) and the agent documentation (`skills/code-engineer/SKILL.md`). The remaining ask is tracked here.

## What's wanted

The session/job UI should show a process-level heartbeat for long-running work — live CPU, RSS, and last-output time — rather than relying on log-file mtime (or a quiet log) alone. Today a long job whose output is block-buffered looks stuck even while the process is busy.

## Scope / approach

TBD — the UI interaction still needs to be decided: where the telemetry lives, what granularity, how often it samples. Design to be confirmed before implementation.

Related: #434, #439.
1000.title: [Feature]Process-level heartbeat (CPU / RSS / last-output) in the session/job UI

1006.author: HongyeZhou
1006.body:
## What happens

The `Binary release (x86_64)` job fails at the very last step, after the artifact is built successfully:

```
Built /home/runner/work/sciencediscovery/sciencediscovery/dist/binary-release/ScienceDiscovery-d255bc9-linux-x86_64 (696.9 MiB, payload f381e6e7b55448e4f127d6fef344dc30)
Release artifact leaks a build-machine path: /home/runner
```

Two occurrences today, both in merge-queue runs for a PR that does not touch packaging (PR #999, which changes `apps/desktop` + `services/api` export saving):

| run | head | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [42491940459](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42491940459) | `fa9878e` | failed, same line |
| [42503143754](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42503143754) | `1c585656` | failed, same line |

The same job passed minutes earlier and later on sibling queue runs ([42505053918](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42505053918) for #1004, [42496441065](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42496441065) for #992), so it is intermittent rather than tied to a head.

Both times the payload scan before it passed: `Payload scan: no build-machine paths found.`

## Why this looks like the gate's own false positive

The gate is `assert_no_release_build_paths()` in `scripts/package-binary-release.sh:94-112`. It greps the whole single-file artifact for `$repository_root`, `$output_dir`, `$HOME` and `$USERPROFILE`. On a GitHub-hosted runner `$HOME` is `/home/runner`.

The payload inside that artifact has already been checked by `assert_no_build_paths()` in `scripts/binary-release/build-payload.sh:144-191`, which deliberately allows two things the artifact-level check cannot:

1. For the `$HOME` needle it excludes `jiuwenswarm/` and `adapter/` (that dependency closure legitimately mentions `/home/runner`).
2. It passes two supplier SBOMs through `scripts/binary-release/filter-upstream-sbom-paths.mjs`, because `pydantic_core-*.dist-info/sboms/pydantic-core.cyclonedx.json` and `watchfiles-*.dist-info/sboms/watchfiles_rust_notify.cyclonedx.json` carry upstream references of the form `path+file:///home/runner/work/pydantic/...` and `path+file:///home/runner/work/watchfiles/...`.

So the payload scan passing tells us the only `/home/runner` occurrences in the payload are the ones it has already ruled acceptable. The artifact-level scan then re-checks those same bytes with no allowance and no way to exclude a subtree, and the only needle that can match is the generic `$HOME` — a bare `/home/runner`, not this build's repository root.

Intermittency fits the layout: the artifact is the pinned `node` binary plus an injected SEA blob plus a `tar | zstd` payload plus a 48-byte footer (`scripts/binary-release/build-binary.mjs:232-262`), so the approved SBOM bytes only appear verbatim when zstd emits that region as a stored block.

## Impact

It blocks the merge queue for PRs that never touch packaging, and each occurrence costs a full payload build (about 9 minutes) plus a queue round-trip. #999 has been kicked out twice today; `merge-gate` goes red as collateral.

## Suggested fix

- Keep the artifact-level check for the build-specific needles only (`$repository_root`, `$output_dir`) — a match there cannot be an upstream coincidence — and drop `$HOME`/`$USERPROFILE` from it, since `build-payload.sh` already covers those with the allowances that a single compressed blob cannot apply.
- Or run the artifact-level check against the decompressed payload (the `--keep-payload` tree) so the SBOM filter can apply to it as well.
- Worth a case in the existing `scripts/binary-release/*.test.mjs` suite: a payload whose only `/home/runner` hits are the two approved SBOM references must pass both checks.

To confirm locally: build with `--keep-payload` and grep the payload tree for `/home/runner`; the hits should be exactly those two SBOMs plus anything under `jiuwenswarm/` or `adapter/`.
1006.title: [Bug] Binary release gate fails on the generic $HOME needle (/home/runner) the payload scan already allows

1007.author: HongyeZhou
1007.body:
## What happens

The `UT` job fails intermittently with one test short of the plan, always in the same place:

```
- ut: status FAIL
- ut: passed 6939 of 6940 planned
- ut: 1 failed
- ut: NODE_WORKER_FAILED: worker-1
- ut: NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED: services/api/src/server.test.ts
- ut: FAIL: services/api/src/server.test.ts::updating SSH credentials immediately probes with the newly stored username and password@linux/amd64
```

`services/api/src/server.test.ts` has already logged `Done 512/605: services/api/src/server.test.ts (180712ms)` earlier in the same run, so the failure is not at an assertion in the test body: it is the file's teardown.

## Occurrences

Four times in one afternoon, on three unrelated PRs, every one of them a different head:

| PR | run | attempt | UT job | named test | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #999 | [42487399804](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42487399804) (merge queue) | 1 | [128752365509](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42487399804/job/128752365509) | `Workspace HTTP writes wait for the active writer and publish refs before returning` | 6909/6910 |
| #734 | [42482149231](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42482149231) | 1 | [128736356154](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42482149231/job/128736356154) | `updating SSH credentials immediately probes with the newly stored username and password` | 6939/6940 |
| #1004 | [42485316924](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42485316924) | 1 | [128745961451](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42485316924/job/128745961451) | `Workspace HTTP writes wait for the active writer and publish refs before returning` | 6906/6907 |
| #999 | [42503143754](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42503143754) (merge queue) | 1 | [128800209585](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42503143754/job/128800209585) | `updating SSH credentials immediately probes with the newly stored username and password` | 6935/6936 |

`#734` attempt 2 and `#1004` attempt 2, on the same commits, passed. Two of the four blocked the merge queue (`merge-gate` goes red as collateral), so each one costs a queue round-trip plus a nine-minute payload/CI re-run.

## Why this is the harness, not the PR under test

- `NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED` is emitted only for a `test:fail` event that carries no per-test token — a file-scope hook or a collection failure, by construction: `test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs:128`.
- `NODE_WORKER_FAILED: worker-1` means the `node --test` worker process for that file exited non-zero: `test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs:195`. So the process died, and the "1 failed" test is the plan's attribution of that, not a failed expectation.
- The named test changes between runs while the file is byte-identical, which a genuine assertion failure in one specific case would not do.
- The four runs span three PRs whose diffs never touch `services/api/src/server.test.ts`, the SSH credential path or the workspace writer path: #734 is configuration capabilities, #1004 is shell-execution settlement, #999 is desktop/API export saving.
- Every occurrence passes on a plain re-run of the same commit.

## Suggested fix

- `server.test.ts` registers many teardown hooks as `context.after(() => new Promise((resolve) => server.close(() => resolve())))` (`:868`, `:872`, `:2578`, `:2582`, `:1933`, ...). `server.close()`'s callback does not fire while an idle keep-alive client socket is still open, so such a hook can hang and take the worker down with it. The file already has the shared `closeApiServer()` helper (`:152`, `:160`) that the rest of the file uses; those hooks should use it too, or pair each `close()` with `closeAllConnections()` the way `:591` does for the adapter.
- The two named tests both start a probe against a stub server. Ending that probe explicitly in the test's own `after` hook, and awaiting it, removes the most likely lingering handle.
- Give the hooks a timeout so a stuck teardown reports the hook and the file by name, instead of surfacing as a worker exit with no reason attached.
- Complementary: have the coordinator include the worker's exit code and signal in the `NODE_WORKER_FAILED` annotation. Right now the only thing a reader gets is `worker-1`, which is what makes every occurrence cost a manual log dig.

Reported from PR review triage; not tied to any single PR.
1007.title: [Bug] UT flakes at server.test.ts teardown: NODE_WORKER_FAILED worker-1 + NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED, 1 of ~6900 failed

1011.author: yuanzhou75
1011.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [X] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [X] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** Nightly real E2E shard `research-12` runs a 46-minute case to completion — `integration: passed`, `total_score: 68.75`, `generation_duration_ms: 2495109` — and then fails in teardown with:

```text
Error: apiRequestContext.fetch: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:4410
```

Nothing was listening on 4410 any more, because the API process behind the adapter had just aborted on V8 heap exhaustion.

**Evidence of the abort.** From the shard's `stack.log` (artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-12`, Nightly run [42519625781](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42519625781), sha `c95f080`):

```text
<--- Last few GCs --->

[5236:0xb123000]  2641988 ms: Scavenge (interleaved) 4020.2 (4116.5) -> 4002.8 (4111.7) MB, pooled: 6 MB, 11.37 / 0.01 ms  (average mu = 0.194, current mu = 0.113) allocation failure;
[5236:0xb123000]  2642420 ms: Mark-Compact 4029.7 (4126.5) -> 3989.8 (4101.4) MB, pooled: 6 MB, 412.69 / 0.01 ms  (average mu = 0.159, current mu = 0.122) task; scavenge might not succeed

FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
...
Aborted (core dumped)
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 134.
```

- The heap dies at **4126.5 MB**, i.e. the Node default old-space limit: no launch path passes `--max-old-space-size` or `NODE_OPTIONS` (`services/api/package.json:9`, `scripts/start-stack.mjs`, `scripts/start-stack.sh`), and nothing in `services/api/src` samples `process.memoryUsage()` or RSS, so the abort arrives with no warning.
- Process uptime at the abort is **2,641,988 ms (~44 min)**, the length of the real case itself.
- After the abort every proxied call turns into `ConnectError` → 502 (`/health`, `/api/models`, `/api/sessions/...`), the adapter shuts down, and teardown cannot reach 4410.

**What this issue previously blamed, and why that was wrong.** An earlier revision named the project plugin event stream (`GET /api/projects/:id/plugins/events`, the adapter's longest-lived request in that run: `phase=body`, `elapsed_ms=2685438`) as the suspected allocation source. That correlation is not a cause and the attribution is withdrawn (review comment [6731433551](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1011#issuecomment-6731433551)):

- that response writes one `event: changed` frame per `PluginControl.changed()` notification plus a `: heartbeat` every 15 s (`services/api/src/plugins/http.ts:23-38`);
- `PluginControl.changed()` is invoked only from settings, project and session mutations — `store.ts:2452,2458,2463,3383,3565,3578,3590,3626,3651,6251` — not per model token or per tool step;
- `control.snapshot(scope)` (`plugins/control.ts:65-69`) is a JSON digest plus a `structuredClone` of the installed plugin list: transient and collectable, and its size does not grow with session length.

So the stream's own writes are kilobytes over 44 minutes. Coalescing frames or caching the snapshot would leave the abort unchanged.

**Where the heap can actually go** (verified at `c95f080`): the API still materialises whole run streams on read paths that are exercised during a long session.

1. `listRunStreamEvents` (`services/api/src/store.ts:6950-6968`) pushes the whole main-run array and every line of the requested stream into `records[]` and only then filters by `after` and sorts — so a replay or reconnect *with* a cursor still allocates the entire stream, twice (array + parsed lines).
2. `exportRunStreams` (`store.ts:6979-6986`) `Promise.all`s that over **every** stream of the run, so the allocations overlap.
3. The plan plugin's `state` query (`services/api/src/plugins/control.ts:114-122`) calls `listRunStreamEvents` **without** `after`, only to keep the `plan.updated` events.
4. `sessionTrajectory` (`services/api/src/trajectory.ts:17-47`) pushes every event of every run and of every subagent/tool stream into a single `events[]` before returning.
5. The file already treats this class as dangerous: `store.ts:7052-7056` says *"A run's stream can reach hundreds of MB. Reading it whole to find the tail allocated the file twice (one string plus the split array) and could exhaust the heap before the process served a single request"* — yet `readStreamLines` (`store.ts:7069-7073`) still accumulates the whole file for the read paths above.

**Missing measurement.** There is no heap profile, RSS/`process.memoryUsage()` timeline, per-stream byte size, or record of which routes were in flight at the abort; the GC lines exist only in the artifact, not in the job log. Without that, the items above stay the better-supported suspects rather than a proven cause, and any fix is unverifiable.

**Expected.**

1. Give the stream read paths a real cursor: filter by `after` **while** streaming lines, never building the whole array; bound or serialise `exportRunStreams`.
2. Let the plan plugin query read only the sequence range it needs, or keep a compact `plan.updated` index instead of the full stream.
3. Bound `sessionTrajectory`: paginate, or stream it to the response.
4. Make the heap budget explicit and observable on every launch path: `--max-old-space-size`, periodic `process.memoryUsage()` logging, and a warning/fatal path before V8 kills the process. A larger cap alone only delays the abort.
5. Land the measurement first (heap snapshot near the limit via `--heapsnapshot-near-heap-limit=1`, an RSS timeline, and the session's stream file sizes), so the fix can be shown to work.

**Impact.** This is not a case-level failure: the case delivered and scored. The gate goes red because teardown talks to a dead process, and `merge-gate` / `Report the outcome` then fail the whole Nightly. The same abort also kills a real user's 46-minute session.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d`; the read paths above are unchanged at `578a9505` (one desktop commit later).
- GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` runner, 15.6 GiB RAM, 4 CPUs; Nightly (`profile: daily`) real E2E, shard `research-12`, started 2026-11-08T20:20:32Z (2026-11-09 04:20 CST).
- Stack: adapter (Python/uvicorn) on `127.0.0.1:4410` in front of the Node API on `4510`, runner on `4411`, memory-graph on `17774`, JiuwenSwarm backend, `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-flash`.
- Case: `TC-E2E-01 research team with custom Specialist and MCP signoff`, 46.1 min.

### Additional Information

**Revision note.** The body was revised after review comment [6731433551](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1011#issuecomment-6731433551): the plugin SSE handler is withdrawn as the target, whole-stream materialisation is promoted to the leading suspect, the missing measurement is stated instead of assumed, and the scope is narrowed to the heap abort.

**Scope.** This issue is the heap abort only. The 89 pending `GET /api/projects/:id/research-package/preview` requests seen in shard `research-8` are not shown to share this cause and are not part of the fix; the teardown behaviour when the API is already dead stays with #1012.

Related: #1012 (the same Nightly, shard `research-8`: an execution stuck in `unknown` making cancel and project delete never return).

### Version Information

- `main` @ `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d`
- Nightly run 42519625781 (2026-11-08T20:20:32Z), shard `research-12`, artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-12` (artifact id 13638505632)
1011.title: [Bug]: A 46-minute real session grows the API heap to the 4 GB default and aborts (exit 134), so teardown meets ECONNREFUSED

1012.author: yuanzhou75
1012.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [X] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [X] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees.** In the Nightly real E2E shard `research-8`, the PUCT-COMPRESS case runs to completion and is scored (`integration_status: passed`, `score: 0.693134`, LLM evaluation `90`) — and then the journey fails in teardown:

```text
Error: DELETE /api/projects/6dfc35df-891e-42c2-b5a5-b89c36d75805 -> 502: {"error":"legacy_unavailable","message":"ReadError","requestId":"762bacad18934c84b5b9dc8ad5c6a09a"}
  at apiJson (test/helpers/journeys.ts:149)
  at cleanupJourney (test/helpers/journeys.ts:1006)
```

A shell execution had been left `unknown` one minute into the run, and from then on the session could neither run a new command nor be torn down: cancelling that execution never returns, and the project delete waits behind it until the adapter's read deadline expires.

**Evidence** (shard `stack.log`, artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-8`, Nightly run [42519625781](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42519625781), sha `c95f080`).

1. The execution that could not be committed:

```text
[jiuwenswarm-bridge] tool run_shell failed: {"executionId":"shell:b8d0dc54332628eb510f7ee6ce92db2d6de9021f2ff429b14e78439eb952b16f","state":"unknown","error":"Existing execution result could not be committed; retry uses the same result","recovery":{"schemaVersion":1,"capability":"unknown","reason":"NOT_REPORTED"},"finalization":"failed",...}
```

2. Every later shell call in that workspace is refused (the agent retried this for the rest of the case):

```text
{"ok":false,"error":{"attempts":1,"code":"TOOL_EXECUTION_FAILED","message":"Execution shell:b8d0dc54... has an unconfirmed outcome. Inspect execution_status before starting more work in this workspace; no replacement was submitted.","retryable":false}}
```

3. At teardown, cancelling exactly that execution never answers — the request line carries no status code at all, i.e. it never completed:

```text
POST /api/sessions/2707a3fe-bb5c-4104-89bf-4a8af4c69ba2/agent-activity/executions/shell%3Ab8d0dc54332628eb510f7ee6ce92db2d6de9021f2ff429b14e78439eb952b16f/cancel HTTP/1.1
```

4. The project delete then trips the adapter's proxy read deadline:

```text
legacy_proxy_failure request_id=762bacad18934c84b5b9dc8ad5c6a09a method=DELETE path=/api/projects/6dfc35df-891e-42c2-b5a5-b89c36d75805 phase=headers elapsed_ms=10350 causes=[{'type': 'ReadError', ...}]
INFO:  127.0.0.1:45568 - "DELETE /api/projects/6dfc35df-891e-42c2-b5a5-b89c36d75805 HTTP/1.1" 502 Bad Gateway
```

5. The API was already parking requests for many minutes in the same window — 89 `GET /api/projects/6dfc35df-891e-42c2-b5a5-b89c36d75805/research-package/preview` requests were still pending at shutdown, the oldest `elapsed_ms=936120` (~15.6 min).

**Code.**

`services/api/src/shell-executions.ts`

- `unavailable()` at 428-464 turns any commit/observation failure into `execution.state = "unknown"`, `provenance = "unconfirmed"`, `finalization = "failed"`, and stores a canned detail built at 451-453 — for this failure the text is `Existing execution result could not be committed; retry uses the same result`, so the underlying error is not visible. The real error is only emitted as a `shell_execution_unconfirmed` warning at 795-796, which did not reach the shard log.
- The commit path at 760-822 (`existingResult` 416-426, `commitFailure` 400-414, fallback 813) is where an execution becomes `unknown` with no transition back to a terminal state.
- The workspace guard that then refuses every new `run_shell` is the "unconfirmed outcome" branch reached from the same record.

Harness side that turns this into a red case: `test/helpers/journeys.ts:995-1010` (`cleanupJourney` → `cancelActiveSessionRuns` → project DELETE) and `test/helpers/session-shutdown.ts:123-131`, which returns `cleanup_failed` whenever runs/executions never go quiet inside its 45 s deadline.

**Expected.**

- An execution whose result cannot be committed must be settlable. Cancelling it must return a definite answer, or cancellation must not be a precondition for the session to go quiet.
- Project deletion must not wait indefinitely on one such execution; a project delete that cannot finish should fail fast with a diagnostic naming the blocker.
- The underlying commit error should be retained on the record (a code plus a short reason), not replaced by the canned sentence, so the next occurrence is diagnosable from `stack.log` alone.
- Today the only recovery is restarting the whole stack, which converts an already-passing real-E2E case into a Nightly failure.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d`.
- GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`, 15.6 GiB RAM; Nightly (`profile: daily`) real E2E, shard `research-8`, started 2026-11-08T20:20:32Z (2026-11-09 04:20 CST).
- Stack: adapter (Python/uvicorn) on `127.0.0.1:4410` in front of the Node API on `4510`, runner on `4411`, memory-graph on `17774`, JiuwenSwarm backend (`CI_E2E_BACKEND=jiuwenswarm`), `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-flash`.
- Case: `PUCT-COMPRESS documented text compression search` (`test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts`), 27.1 min; run metrics: `integration_status: passed`, `score 0.693134`, `baseline_gate_score 0.285339`.

### Additional Information

This is not a one-off: on the same Nightly, `research-5` also failed with the harness giving up on a 5 s read (`apiRequestContext.fetch: Timeout 5000ms exceeded`), and `research-12` was killed by an API heap OOM (issue #1011). A plausible shared cause is that long real sessions accumulate work the API never bounds; this issue is the part that makes teardown unrecoverable once one execution is stuck.

### Version Information

- `main` @ `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d`
- Nightly run 42519625781 (2026-11-08T20:20:32Z), shard `research-8`, artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-8` (artifact id 13636806778)
1012.title: [Bug]: A shell execution whose result cannot be committed stays unknown forever, and its cancel / project delete never return

1018.author: yuanzhou75
1018.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

A session can become **permanently un-exportable** after one of its shell executions gets stuck in the provenance-commit recovery loop. The recovery loop rewrites the session's execution record every few seconds, and the export revision hashes that file's mtime/ctime, so the revision never stabilizes: the preview never leaves `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING`, and every export attempt fails with `导出期间会话内容发生变化，请基于最新内容重新导出。`

This makes both 必要导出 and 完整导出 unusable for that session — the user has no way out except editing the data directory.

### Evidence

Session `dcfe6ace-c7d1-45c7-a781-9928f5c29c0e` (project `04a09bcd-a2f5-4ef9-a17a-3f9ef43a75ff`), build `c95f080a`:

```text
GET /api/projects/{pid}/research-package/preview?sessionId=dcfe6ace…&level=necessary
  → 409 {"code":"EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING"} repeatedly (observed 6/6, and 3/4 in an earlier run)

POST /api/projects/{pid}/research-package/exports  (with the revision that finally returned)
  → 202 … then
  → failed "导出期间会话内容发生变化，请基于最新内容重新导出。"
```

Two consecutive previews returned **different** revisions for the same unchanged session (`803b8ecf…`, `05794da2…`, `1381d7ef…`, `e7551a38…`), while a control session that has no stuck execution kept the **same** revision across four previews over 45 s (`411c6ccb…` ×4).

The churn source — `data/execution-runs/<sessionId>.json` is rewritten continuously:

```text
2026-11-09 12:56:09.510   (size unchanged, 4826 bytes)
2026-11-09 12:56:17.530
2026-11-09 12:56:25.562
```

and the execution responsible is the one from the finalization-401 case in #978:

```text
id:            shell:30b80e039b1649cbb900d4ff512b5c2b09ea89bd95c55151d1f9c8a2f3c46236
accepted:      true
provenance:    unconfirmed
finalization:  failed
finishedAt:    null
observation:   {"status":"blocked","failureCount":1,
                "nextRetryAt":"2026-11-09T04:56:34.553Z",
                "lastError":{"code":"PROVENANCE_COMMIT_FAILED",…}}
```

`services/api/src/shell-executions.ts` reschedules it (`configureRecovery` → `reconcilePending` every 1 s, retry backoff ~8 s), each retry rewrites the execution record.

Relevant revision inputs in `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts` (`previewRevision`): it hashes `files` (every file under `store.sessionDataPaths(session.id)` with `size`/`mtimeMs`/`ctimeMs`) **and** `shells: store.shellExecutions.snapshot(session.id)` — so a forever-retrying execution invalidates the revision on every tick.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Produce a session whose shell execution ends in `PROVENANCE_COMMIT_FAILED` (e.g. the finalization-401 path from #978 — in this data set it came from a run that ran `run_shell` and then hit the 401 on finalization).
2. Open 更多会话操作 → 导出会话 and watch the size preview: it keeps saying 正在计算范围与大小… and never settles.
3. Start an export anyway; it fails with 导出期间会话内容发生变化.
4. Compare with a session whose executions all committed — its preview settles in seconds and exports fine.

### Expected

- Export must be able to snapshot a session whose execution is stuck in recovery: either exclude volatile recovery bookkeeping (`observation.nextRetryAt`, lease timestamps) from the revision, or take the revision from committed/stable fields only, and let packaging succeed with the last known execution state (marked as such).
- A session with a stuck execution should not be permanently un-exportable; the recovery loop should reach a terminal state (or back off without rewriting the record every tick).

### Observed

- `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING` forever, then a revision that changes under the export, so packaging always aborts with "会话内容发生变化".
- No user-facing explanation that the block is caused by an execution stuck in recovery.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

```text
Host        Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04, local source checkout
Mode        ./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local (adapter :4310, API :4410, runner :4311, memory-graph :17674)
Node v22.23.4, pnpm 11.1.2, uv 0.13.7, Python 3.12
Model       glm-5.2 over an OpenAI-compatible relay
Data dir    ~/sciencediscovery/.sciencediscovery-data (evolve runs + science memory present in this session)
```

## Additional Information

Related: #978 (the finalization 401 that leaves the execution `accepted=true / provenance unconfirmed` — this report is the export-side consequence), #995 (import opens two sessions), #803 (the feature).

The same session also demonstrates that evolve runs are not carried by the package; that is filed separately.

## Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- Tested commit: `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d` (main, 2026-11-08T18:06:21Z)
1018.title: [Bug]: Session export becomes impossible when a shell execution is stuck in the provenance-commit recovery loop

1019.author: yuanzhou75
1019.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

A research package does **not** capture the session's **evolve runs**. The package carries only the evolve result files (`evolve/<runId>/candidate.py`, because they are ordinary artifacts), so after import the session's evolve content is gone: `GET /api/evolve/runs?sessionId=…` returns an empty list, and the Evolve panel has nothing to show — no search tree, no candidate scores, no token/budget record, no baseline, no candidate history.

Importing an evolve session back therefore does **not** reproduce the evolve content, which is exactly what a user expects from “导出会话 → 导入会话” when the session used `/evolve-design`.

### Evidence

Source session `fe1ef6bf-e61a-49c2-a62f-75904a37a375` (project `299bc26a-6e56-46d7-a977-5d4e3c264aaa`), build `c95f080a`:

```text
source evolve runs:
  83cbb6de  status=succeeded candidates=20 tokens=171084
  a539ffc0  status=succeeded candidates=20 tokens=95575
source artifacts:
  evolve/83cbb6de/candidate.py  v2
  evolve/a539ffc0/candidate.py  v2
```

Exported with 必要导出 (`level=necessary`, 109,724-byte package) and imported into a fresh project:

```text
records.json top-level keys:
  ["exportLevel","exportProfile","project","sessions","artifacts",
   "environmentRevisions","versionObjects","memoryGraph"]
records keys containing "evolv": []          ← no evolve dimension at all

imported session 4e9d0664-ae6c-499a-b154-5343791153f9:
  GET /api/evolve/runs?sessionId=4e9d0664…  → []        (0 runs)
  artifacts                                 → evolve/83cbb6de/candidate.py v2,
                                              evolve/a539ffc0/candidate.py v2   (restored)
```

So the candidate files survive as artifacts while the run records — the thing that makes them meaningful — do not.

Root cause in code: `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts` builds `records` as `{ exportLevel, exportProfile, project, sessions, artifacts, environmentRevisions, versionObjects, memoryGraph|memoryGraphSummary }`. The session record (`services/api/src/research-package-history.ts`) exports `executionRuns`, `messages`, `runs`, `workspace`, `validations`, `trajectory`, … but nothing from `store.dataDir/evolution/*` (runs / ledger / results / programs). `countExport(...)` likewise has no evolve counter, which is why the preview's included/omitted numbers never mention evolve content either.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run an evolve-design case so the session has one or two evolve runs (each with candidates and a candidate.py artifact).
2. 更多会话操作 → 导出会话 → 必要导出 (or 完整导出), save the package.
3. Import the package into a new project.
4. Open the imported session: the messages and the `evolve/<runId>/candidate.py` artifacts are there, but the Evolve panel and `GET /api/evolve/runs?sessionId=…` show nothing.

### Expected

After importing a session that used evolve, the imported (read-only) snapshot shows the same evolve runs as the source: run id, algorithm, status, candidate count, scores/best candidate, token/cost budget and baseline; and continuing research from it keeps that evolve content available. If a run cannot be reproduced byte-for-byte, the import should at least list it as an explicit omission instead of silently dropping it.

### Observed

- `records` has no evolve section; the import receipt lists no evolve omission either, so the loss is silent.
- Imported session reports zero evolve runs; only `evolve/<runId>/candidate.py` artifacts remain.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

```text
Host        Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04, local source checkout
Mode        ./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local (adapter :4310, API :4410, runner :4311, evolve sidecar, memory-graph :17674)
Node v22.23.4, pnpm 11.1.2, uv 0.13.7, Python 3.12
Model       glm-5.2 over an OpenAI-compatible relay
Case        docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md (compress/decompress, stdlib only)
```

## Additional Information

Science memory **is** carried: the same necessary package contains `memoryGraph` with 20 nodes / 19 relationships, and after import the snapshot reports the same 20/19 (verified through the export preview of the imported session). So the gap is specific to evolve.

Related: #995 (import opens two sessions), #803 (feature), and the export-blocking issue filed separately for sessions whose executions are stuck in recovery. A separate observation from the same test: 完整导出 with both “包含完整轨迹详情” and “包含完整科学记忆图谱” fails for this session with `Research package exceeds the archive size limit` (`MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 512 MB` in `packages/research-package/src/index.ts`), while plain 完整导出 succeeds (20.2 MB compressed, 933 MB estimated uncompressed).

## Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- Tested commit: `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d` (main, 2026-11-08T18:06:21Z)
1019.title: [Bug]: Research package does not carry evolve runs, so an imported session loses all evolve content (only candidate.py artifacts survive)

1021.author: yuanzhou75
1021.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

While a shell execution sits in the provenance-commit retry loop, **every attempt rewrites `data/execution-runs/<sessionId>.json` even though the file's bytes never change**. The rewrite replaces the file (new inode) and moves `mtime`/`ctime`, so anything that watches those timestamps sees constant change in a session whose content is static.

This is the root cause behind the export-revision churn in #1018. PR #1020 makes the export revision immune to it (a content digest instead of `size`/`mtime`/`ctime`, plus a stable shell projection) and explicitly calls itself a defence, not a cure. This issue tracks the wasted write itself.

### Evidence

Session `dcfe6ace-c7d1-45c7-a781-9928f5c29c0e`, build `c95f080a`, local stack. The file is rewritten every ~10 s, alternating between two inodes (each write is a temp file plus replace), and every sample has the same 4,826 bytes and the same digest:

```text
2026-11-09 13:32:40.870   inode 45097   4826 bytes
2026-11-09 13:32:50.922   inode 45093   4826 bytes
2026-11-09 13:33:00.890   inode 45097   4826 bytes
2026-11-09 13:33:10.894   inode 45093   4826 bytes
2026-11-09 13:33:20.914   inode 45097   4826 bytes
2026-11-09 13:33:30.930   inode 45093   4826 bytes

two samples 12 s apart:  4826 bytes  md5 59a848023ad12930497826a781aed049  (identical)
```

The content is three records and the last one is already settled — `id: shell:30b80e…`, `status: succeeded`, `finishedAt: 2026-11-08T08:47:32.158Z` — while the shell execution itself is `accepted: true`, `provenance: unconfirmed`, `finalization: failed`, `observation.lastError.code = PROVENANCE_COMMIT_FAILED`. So the ledger write succeeds and the attempt fails afterwards, and the next attempt rewrites the same bytes.

The same churn appeared in the #1018 report as `12:56:09.510 / 12:56:17.530 / 12:56:25.562`, all 4,826 bytes.

### Root cause

1. The recovery loop's `finalize` handler is `commitExistingShellExecutionResult` (`services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts:664`, `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts:319`).
2. `commitExistingShellExecutionResult` (`packages/provenance/src/recorder.ts:997-1050`) computes a `resultDigest`, loads the settled row, and **only throws when an existing digest differs** (`:1020-1022`). When the digest matches it keeps going and appends the run again (`:1037`). There is no "already committed, return" path — `adoptShellOutcome` in the same file does have one (`:1139-1146`).
3. `store.appendExecutionRun` **does** detect the duplicate and returns from the mutator without pushing (`services/api/src/store.ts:7143-7146`), so the array is unchanged.
4. But `mutateArray` calls `writeArray` unconditionally (`services/api/src/store.ts:2233-2237`), and `writeArray` always writes a temp file and replaces the target (`:2213-2225`). Hence new inode, new `mtime`/`ctime`, byte-identical content.

Verified from code and the samples above; the ~10 s cadence is inferred from the record shape (the settled row exists while the attempt still fails), nobody has captured a stack trace — `/proc/<pid>/io` is unreadable and ptrace is unavailable in this environment.

## Proposed fixes (two independent options, different risk)

**A. Short-circuit in the recorder — low risk.** After computing `resultDigest`, if `existing?.resultDigest === resultDigest`, return the result instead of re-appending. This is the same idempotency check `adoptShellOutcome` already uses, and it only skips work that is provably a no-op. Nothing else reads a bumped `mtime` for this file legitimately.

**B. Skip no-op writes in `mutateArray` — wide blast radius, needs its own evaluation.** Snapshot the array before the operation and skip `writeArray` when nothing changed. This removes the whole class of empty writes (`messages`, `sessionRuns`, `artifactPlans`, `artifactReviews`, `claims`, … all go through `mutateArray`), but it changes write semantics for every array the store owns: cross-process visibility, the `replaceFile` retry story, and any reader that uses `mtime` invalidation (the research-package revision did exactly that) would need to be re-checked. It also needs a test that a genuine change still writes.

A alone fixes this report; B is the broader cleanup and should not ride along with a bug fix.

## Expected

- Re-committing a shell execution whose settled row and digest already exist leaves `execution-runs/<sessionId>.json` untouched — same inode, same `mtime`.
- A retry loop can never produce disk writes for state that has not changed.

## Observed

- One write every ~10 s forever: ~8,600 redundant rewrites per day for this single session, each with a `fsync`-worthy replace, and a continuously moving `ctime`.
- Anything hashing `size`/`mtime`/`ctime` of session data never converges while the execution is stuck (this is how #1018 was produced).

## Detailed Environment Information Description

```text
Host        Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04, local source checkout
Mode        ./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local (adapter :4310, API :4410, runner :4311, memory-graph :17674)
Node v22.23.4, pnpm 11.1.2, uv 0.13.7, Python 3.12
Data dir    ~/sciencediscovery/.sciencediscovery-data
Session     dcfe6ace-c7d1-45c7-a781-9928f5c29c0e (project 04a09bcd-a2f5-4ef9-a17a-3f9ef43a75ff)
```

## Additional Information

Related: #1018 (the export-side consequence this write produces), #1012 (the execution that never settles), #978 (the finalization 401 behind it), and PR #1020 (defence: content-digest revision, does not change the writer).

## Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- Tested commit: `c95f080a6c3b1bb5e020808b5114e1894148422d` (main, 2026-11-08T18:06:21Z)
1021.title: [Bug]: A failed shell finalization rewrites execution-runs/<session>.json with byte-identical content on every retry

1023.author: JinhZhao
1023.body:
## Summary

`POST /trace/provenance` returns HTTP 503 `memory_graph_query_limit` on a research session graph of ~3200 nodes / ~4560 edges. The query deterministically exhausts the local Cypher interpreter's work budget (250,000 units) before producing any result.

The budget protection mechanism itself is sound and necessary — it prevents unbounded queries from locking the server. The issue is that `get_trace()` has no internal bounding (per-hop node cap, depth limit within a hop, or early termination) that would allow it to return a partial or approximate result within the budget. By contrast, the analogous `/query/chain-exists` endpoint succeeds on the same graph because its hop table uses explicit per-entry limits.

## Reproduction

1. Run a literature research session that produces ~3000+ nodes in the Memory Graph (a single session with search + evidence + claims is sufficient).
2. Call `POST /trace/provenance` with `{"node_id": "<evidence_id>", "target_label": "ResearchGoal"}`.
3. Observe 503 response with `{"detail":{"code":"memory_graph_query_limit",...}}`.

The failure is deterministic and scope-independent — `max_hops: 1` and `target_label: "WebPage"` both still trigger it.

## Measured Evidence

Memory graph log shows 9 budget exhaustion events across a 3+ hour session, all with identical signature:

```
work=250001 traversals=29324 reason=CypherBudgetExceeded
```

Graph scale grew from 3188 to 3222 nodes during this window. The work count and traversal count are identical regardless of graph size or query parameters — the budget is consumed by the first hop's unbounded variable-depth expansion.

Query duration is 109-139 ms in all cases — the 10-second time budget (`_MAX_QUERY_SECONDS`) is never the trigger; the work budget always hits first.

Zero successful `trace` queries were logged during the entire session. Single-kind `chain-exists` queries on the same graph succeed consistently.

## Why chain-exists Succeeds Where trace Fails

`get_trace()` uses the `_CHAIN_HOPS` table (query.py:2048-2207), which is documented in code as "retained" / "deprecated" but remains the active implementation for trace queries. Each source label has 4-8 upstream hop entries with unbounded variable-depth patterns (`"1.."`) and no per-entry node limit.

`/query/chain-exists` uses `_BUTTON_CHAIN_HOPS` (query.py:1888-2039), where each button kind has 1-4 curated hop entries with bounded depth (`"1"`) and explicit `limit` caps (typically `limit=1`).

| Aspect | `get_trace()` / `_CHAIN_HOPS` | `chain-exists` / `_BUTTON_CHAIN_HOPS` |
|---|---|---|
| Hop entries per label | 4-8 | 1-4 |
| Depth specifier | `"1.."` (unbounded) | `"1"` (bounded) |
| Per-entry node limit | None | `limit=1` typical |
| All-or-nothing short-circuit | No | Yes |
| Payload per hop | Full node + elementId + labels | `collect(DISTINCT elementId)` only |
| Result on 3200-node graph | 503 budget exceeded | 200 OK |

## Impact

The trace endpoint is the backend for the reviewer authenticity trace UI and the graph-explorer provenance button. On any session that includes a literature search subgraph (which is the normal use case for the product), these features are non-functional.

The budget is a hardcoded module-level constant (`_cypher.py:57`: `_MAX_QUERY_WORK = 250_000`). It is not configurable via environment variable, config file, or constructor parameter. This means operators cannot tune it for their graph scale — the only outcomes are success (small graphs) or 503 (moderate+ graphs).

## Code Identity Verification

The `sciencediscovery_memory_graph` package is byte-identical between SD and the CatalystPIDecision fork:

| File | SHA256 | Match |
|---|---|---|
| `_cypher.py` | `ea4a50cea4cdb0b1ac35178fa61ba5dd02ce5d2180b158c0cc2b66e1f0c03eeb` | Identical |
| `query.py` | `3de4bc994750a4cc6f759a0d4fd380cadd53820066e41ae847a0bb8da29cde9a` | Identical |

This issue is filed against SD upstream because the affected code originates there.

## Suggested Improvements

1. **Add per-hop node cap to `get_trace()`**: Limit collected nodes per hop entry (e.g., 50 nodes), consistent with the `_BUTTON_CHAIN_HOPS` pattern. This would allow trace to return partial results within budget.

2. **Migrate `get_trace()` from `_CHAIN_HOPS` to a bounded hop table**: The `_CHAIN_HOPS` table is documented as deprecated. Replacing it with a curated, bounded hop table (similar to `_BUTTON_CHAIN_HOPS`) would align trace with the pattern that already works for chain-exists.

3. **Graceful degradation in `/trace/provenance` handler**: Return a partial result with `truncated: true, reason: "budget_exceeded"` instead of 503, so the UI can display what was reached.

4. **Make budget configurable**: Expose `_MAX_QUERY_WORK` via environment variable or server constructor parameter, so operators can tune for their graph scale without code changes.

## Not Requested

This issue does not request removal or increase of the budget constant. The budget protection is a necessary safeguard. The request is for the trace query pattern to operate within the existing budget on moderate-size graphs, and for a degradation path when it cannot.

---

**Environment**: Memory Graph local backend, graph scale 3188-3222 nodes / 4527-4570 edges, single literature research session with 6 Evidence + 5 Claim nodes. Reproduced consistently over 30+ minutes with deterministic budget exhaustion.
1023.title: C:/Users/win11/.qoder/bin/git/trace/provenance returns 503 memory_graph_query_limit on sessions with search subgraphs

1024.author: yuanzhou75
1024.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

Exporting a session works today, but the dialog is still shaped like a developer tool rather than a user task. Everything a user needs in order to decide *what* they are handing off, *how big* it will be, and *what happened* to the last export is either missing, misleading, or only reachable by reopening a modal. This is the session-export UI design work, desktop first.

The save flow itself was fixed in #986 / PR #999 (native save dialog, automatic save, per-export tracking) and the capability is specified in #803, so this issue is not about those. It is about the presentation of scope, size, progress and outcome.

Observations from the current desktop UI (`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`, main 2026-11-09) and from a real export of a session with evolve runs and scientific memory (build `c95f080a`):

| What the user sees | What is actually true | Why it misleads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 预计大小（未压缩）**910.6 MiB** on the 完整导出 card | the saved `.sdresearch` was **19.2 MiB** (20,161,641 bytes) | one number, 46× the real file; it is `estimateKind: "uncompressed"` and the label is the only hint |
| no size limit anywhere in the dialog | the archive cap is **512 MiB**, checked against the *compressed* archive (`packages/research-package/src/index.ts:15`, `:231`) | the one size shown cannot be compared with the limit that decides success |
| 完整导出 + 包含完整轨迹详情 + 包含完整科学记忆图谱 → packaging runs, then fails | `Research package exceeds the archive size limit`, in **English**, inside a zh-CN UI | minutes of packaging for an outcome that was predictable, plus an untranslated, unactionable message |
| 正在计算范围与大小… forever, primary button disabled | `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING`, retried every 1.5 s with no cap and no explanation (`ResearchPackage.tsx:217-227`) | no reason, no retry, no cancel, no way to know whether waiting helps (#1018) |
| a single line `N 个导出进行中`, expandable to filenames | phases (packaging / saving) and destination are known to the client but not shown | the user cannot tell "still packing" from "packed, now writing to disk" |
| cancelling your own export | `pushFlash("error", t.exportCanceled)` — a red error (`:152`, `:271`, `:350`) | a deliberate user action is reported as a failure |
| 已保存的会话包 list inside the export modal | the list is component state only; the shell persists just `lastExportDir` (`win_desktop/src/export-state.ts`) | after restarting the app the history is gone, and "打开文件位置" cannot be used for an earlier package |
| 导出会话 only in the session row menu (`Sidebar.tsx:210`) | — | a first-class task is buried three levels down |
| import dialog: title, object count, `omissions` | per-dimension content is unavailable (`PackageInspection` has no counts) | the user cannot see what will be restored before committing; this is also how evolve runs disappear silently (#1019) |

### Design Ideas

**1. Make the choice about content, not about jargon.** Replace the two profile cards' taglines with a per-dimension table for the selected profile — 会话 / 消息 / 产物 / 产物版本 / 工作区文件 / 执行记录 / 任务 / 科学记忆节点 / 关系 — and render the two optional switches nested under 完整导出 with their *delta* shown on the same table and on the size line. The server already computes these numbers (`countExport`, with Chinese labels in `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:444`); the preview payload simply does not expose them yet.

**2. Show two honest numbers and the limit.** `未压缩 ≈ 910.6 MiB` is useful for disk planning; `归档 ≈ 19.2 MiB` is what the user copies around and what the cap applies to. Show the archive limit as a meter, and once a package exists show its real archive size. Before packaging, if the selection is over the limit, say so on the card and offer the fix (drop 完整轨迹 / 完整记忆图谱, or switch to 必要导出) instead of starting a task that must fail.

**3. A durable export center instead of a transient modal.** Turn the export surface into a panel/sheet with two blocks: the scope form above, a persistent list below (filename, archive size, time, state, destination, 打开文件位置, 重新保存). The list must survive closing the panel and restarting the app, and `已取消` must be a neutral state, not a red error. Keep the modal as the confirmation step if a modal is still wanted; keeping state in component memory is what loses it.

**4. Explain blocked and pending states.** When the preview cannot settle, say why in user terms ("该会话有一个执行停在恢复流程，导出范围暂不可确定" is the #1018 case), and offer 重试 / 取消 / 查看该执行. A disabled primary button with a spinner is not a state.

**5. Give the task a first-class entry.** A 导出 button in the session header (`SessionBar`), with the row-menu item kept as a shortcut. Import stays where it is.

**6. Localize and make failures actionable.** Server errors reach the UI untranslated (`task.error` is rendered raw at `:321` and flashed at `:153`). Map known failures (archive limit, changed revision, missing task, preview pending) to zh-CN copy with a next step; keep the raw string behind a details disclosure, consistent with the failure-alert principle in #846.

**7. Import side, same information standard.** Show the same per-dimension counts from the package manifest in the inspect step, plus an explicit "不会恢复" block (this is where an evolve omission must appear, #1019), so the user decides before importing rather than discovering an empty Evolve panel afterwards.

Alternatives not selected: restyling the existing modal without changing what it shows; auto-selecting 完整导出; removing the size estimate entirely (users need it for disk planning); moving export into the settings page.

### Involved Public APIs

Additive only, no breaking change:

- `GET /api/projects/{projectId}/research-package/preview` — add `counts` (same shape as `countExport`), `archiveLimitBytes`, and if a cheap estimate is acceptable `estimatedArchiveBytes`. Keep `estimateKind` so a client never mistakes the two.
- `POST .../research-package/exports` and `GET .../exports/{id}` — expose the finished archive size (`archiveBytes`) so the list can show it without a download.
- `POST .../research-package/inspect` — expose the manifest `counts` already present in the package manifest.

`apps/web` and `apps/desktop` share `apps/desktop/src/api/research-package.ts` shapes, so both must keep working; web keeps the browser-download destination, desktop keeps the token-bound native save.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx` | Scope form, counts table, size meter, export center, localized failures |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/SessionBar.tsx`, `Sidebar.tsx`, `App.tsx` | Entry point and panel wiring |
| `apps/desktop/src/styles/research-package.css`, `text/zh.ts`, `text/en.ts` | Layout and copy, both languages |
| `win_desktop` (`export-state.ts`, `preload.ts`, `main.ts`) | Persisted export list, destination tokens, reveal-in-folder |
| `services/api` (`research-snapshots.ts`) | Preview payload, counts, limit, archive size |
| `packages/research-package` | `MAX_TOTAL_BYTES`, manifest counts, omission strings |
| `apps/web` | Same view; parity required but not the focus |

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Component tests for the new blocks: counts table renders server counts; the size block shows both numbers and never labels the archive size as the estimate; an over-limit selection warns before `startExport` is called; cancel renders neutral; unknown server errors fall back to the raw string behind details.
- E2E on the desktop build with the real local stack, using a session that has evolve runs and scientific memory (the fixture from #1019):
  - 必要导出 and 完整导出 each round-trip to a saved `.sdresearch`, and the counts shown in the dialog match `POST .../inspect` of the produced package.
  - 完整导出 with both switches on the oversized session shows the pre-flight warning instead of a late English failure.
  - restart the app: the export list still shows the saved package and 打开文件位置 works.
  - cancel during packaging and during saving: neutral state, no error flash.
  - preview blocked (session with a stuck execution): the dialog explains the reason and offers retry/cancel.
- Import: inspect shows counts and the explicit not-restored list; compare against the live imported session.
- Commands: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build`, `pnpm ci:l1`. Screenshots of the export panel (necessary, complete with switches, over-limit warning, export list after restart) go in the PR body for the owner's visual approval, per the UI review rule.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The export scope step shows per-dimension counts for the selected profile, and the two optional switches show their effect on those counts and on size.
- [ ] The size block shows the uncompressed estimate and the archive size/limit distinctly; no single number is presented as the file the user will copy.
- [ ] A selection that cannot fit the archive limit is reported before packaging, with the fix offered on the card.
- [ ] Progress shows per-task state (packaging / saving) and destination; the export list survives closing the panel and restarting the app, and 打开文件位置 works for earlier packages.
- [ ] Cancelling a self-initiated export is neutral, not an error; known failures are localized with an actionable next step, raw text only behind details.
- [ ] A blocked preview names its cause and offers retry/cancel.
- [ ] Import inspection shows the same per-dimension counts and an explicit "will not be restored" list.
- [ ] Both zh-CN and en copy exist; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck|test|build` and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.
- [ ] The owner has seen the screenshots in the PR body before approval.

### Additional Information

Related: #803 (feature scope), #986 (save flow, closed by PR #999), #846 (localized, non-redundant failure presentation), #1018 (a session whose preview never settles — the blocked-state copy is a product decision there), #1019 (evolve runs absent from the package — the import "will not be restored" block must state it), #995 (import opens two sessions), #801 (desktop scientific memory), #798 (desktop evolve).

Measured numbers quoted above come from one real session on build `c95f080a`: 完整导出 preview 933,095,424 bytes uncompressed → saved archive 20,161,641 bytes; 完整导出 with both switches → `Research package exceeds the archive size limit`. The failure is not reproduced by any test in this issue description; it was observed by hand.
